text:
Buffalo won 5-3, but Florida probably played the better game. The Panthers out-attempted the Sabres 63 to 49, and the simulated replays of every shot give them the win 57 percent of the time. Total expected goals were nearly even (3.63 to 3.48). The Sabres' edge came at even strength, where they held a 2.33 to 1.23 advantage in chance quality, and they built it with a 1.50 to 0.73 first period before Florida took over the middle of the game.

That swing showed up on the scoreboard. Josh Doan opened the scoring at 5:58 of the first, Anton Lundell tied it, and Rasmus Dahlin put Buffalo ahead on a power-play slap shot. In the second, Sam Reinhart scored twice with the man advantage, the first a 88 percent chance from close range, and Florida piled up 1.70 expected goals to Buffalo's 1.00. Ryan McLeod's wrist shot in between put the Sabres back in front, but Reinhart's second tied it at 3-3. Reinhart finished with 1.28 individual expected goals, the best number on either roster.

Buffalo won it on the margins. Noah Ostlund's power-play goal made it 4-3 early in the third, and Tage Thompson added the fifth at 13:20. Both Florida goalies finished below expectation, with Akira Schmid at minus 1.27 goals saved above expected, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 13 of 14 for plus 0.87. Owen Power logged 26:30 with two assists, and Buffalo's chance share ran strongly in its favor whenever he was on the ice.
